extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of crystallography, mineralogy, and geology
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and descriptive criteria for identifying, naming, and classifying crystals by their crystal system, symmetry class, axial parameters, and characteristic forms (indices, faces, open/closed forms, enantiomorphism). Useful for diagnosing specimen forms and assigning Miller indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of crystal systems by axial relations
rubrics_metrics.description: A crystal system is defined by the relationships between its three crystallographic axes (angles and relative lengths). Examples: cubic (a : a : a; all axes equal and at right angles), tetragonal (a : a : c; two equal horizontal axes with a different vertical axis), orthorhombic (a : b : c; three mutually perpendicular unequal axes), monoclinic (two right angles, one oblique; a : b : c with beta angle), anorthic/triclinic (no right angles, unequal lengths; require a:b:c and alpha, beta, gamma), hexagonal/rhombohedral (special arrangements with triad/hexad axes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The axial parameters (ratios and angles) are characteristic constants for all crystals of a given substance in a given system and are used to determine and distinguish the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axial ratio as characteristic constant
rubrics_metrics.description: The axial ratio (e.g., a:c in tetragonal, a:b:c in orthorhombic) is constant for crystals of the same substance and characteristic of that substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cassiterite c = 0.67232 (a taken as unity); anatase c = 1.7771. Use measured axial ratios to help identify substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miller indices notation and meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Crystal faces are indexed using Miller indices in braces {hkl} referring to the intercepts with crystallographic axes; in hexagonal axes a four-index notation {hikl} is used with h + i + k = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific index sets correspond to named forms (e.g., cube {100}, octahedron {111}, rhombic dodecahedron {110}). The indices encode orientation and intercepts and are essential for naming and comparing forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open form vs closed form
rubrics_metrics.description: An open form does not enclose space and therefore can exist only in combination with other forms; a closed form encloses space by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: tetragonal prism {110} is an open form and occurs only combined with other forms, whereas tetragonal bipyramids are closed forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: General form criterion ({hkl} with unequal indices)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'general form' of a class is the form where all intercept indices are unequal (written {hkl}); it typically has the maximum number of faces for that class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: hexakis-octahedron (general cubic form) has indices all unequal and 48 faces; ditetragonal bipyramid is the general tetragonal form bounded by sixteen scalene triangles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holohedral vs hemihedral (and hemihedral variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Holohedral forms have the full set of faces consistent with the symmetry of the class; hemihedral (hemihedral/hemihedral-with-parallel/inclined faces) forms have only half the number of faces or modified face arrangements derived from holohedral forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From holohedral forms two hemihedral forms (positive and negative) may be derived by suppressing alternate faces; hemihedral faces often differ in surface character and orientation from the holohedral equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enantiomorphism (right- and left-handed forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some pairs of forms are geometrically similar but nonsuperposable mirror images (enantiomorphous). They may be designated positive or negative (e.g., {111} vs {1'11}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enantiomorphous crystals can differ in face character and may rotate the plane of polarized light; examples include two tetrahedra {111} and {1'11}, and pentagonal icositetrahedra that are right- or left-handed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cubic system definition and characteristic forms
rubrics_metrics.description: In the cubic system the three axes are equal and at right angles (parameters a : a : a). Common simple fixed forms include the cube {100}, octahedron {111}, and rhombic dodecahedron {110}; in some cubic forms the angles and indices are fixed, in others they may vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many minerals (iron, copper, silver, gold, garnet, etc.) crystallize in cubic forms. Variable-faced cubic forms (triakis-, tetra-, hexakis- variants) generate series of indices (e.g., {hhk}, {hkk}, {hko}, {hkl}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Triakis-octahedron identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Triakis-octahedron is bounded by twenty-four isosceles triangles and can be viewed as an octahedron with a low triangular pyramid on each face; indices occur as {221}, {331}, {332}, etc., or generically {hhk}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclinations of faces may vary, producing a series of forms; this aids visual identification on crystals where triangular pyramidal protuberances exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Icositetrahedron identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Icositetrahedron (sometimes called 'trapezohedron') is bounded by twenty-four trapezoidal faces; indices include {211}, {311}, {322}, or generically {hkk}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analcite, leucite, and garnet often crystallize in simple {211} icositetrahedron; combinations with other cubic forms are common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tetrakis-hexahedron identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Tetrakis-hexahedron is bounded by twenty-four isosceles triangles grouped in fours over the cube faces; indices are {210}, {310}, {320}, or generically {hko}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different inclinations of faces yield forms approximating cube or rhombic dodecahedron; faces are parallel to one crystallographic axis and intercept the other axes in different lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hexakis-octahedron as maximal simple cubic form
rubrics_metrics.description: Hexakis-octahedron replaces each octahedron face by six scalene triangles, totaling forty-eight faces — the greatest number of faces possible for any simple form in crystals; indices are generally {hkl} with all unequal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms usually appear in combination with other cubic forms; {421} has been observed as a simple form on fluorspar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tetrahedral class symmetry characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Tetrahedral class lacks a centre of symmetry and cubic planes of symmetry; tetrad axes become dyad axes and the four triad axes are polar (different faces at their two ends); other symmetry elements may be similar to other cubic subclasses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some simple forms (cube, rhombic dodecahedron, tetrakis-hexahedron) are geometrically similar to holohedral equivalents, but face surface characters differ (e.g., striation patterns). Other forms are hemihedral with half the faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tetrahedron form identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The tetrahedron is bounded by four equilateral triangles (regular tetrahedron); the angles between normals of faces are 109°28'. It can be derived by suppressing alternate faces of the octahedron.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indices typically {111}; used to recognize tetrahedral growth forms like diamond, blende.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deltoid dodecahedron identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Deltoid dodecahedron is the hemihedral form of the triakis-octahedron, bounded by twelve trapezoidal faces and with indices {hhk}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize by trapezoidal faces and reduced face count relative to the holohedral parent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triakis-tetrahedron and hexakis-tetrahedron identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Triakis-tetrahedron is the hemihedral form {hkk} of the icositetrahedron, bounded by twelve isosceles triangles in threes over tetrahedron faces. Hexakis-tetrahedron is the hemihedral form {hkl} of the hexakis-octahedron, bounded by twenty-four scalene triangles and being the general form of the class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use face count and arrangement (grouped triangles over tetrahedral faces) to distinguish these hemihedral tetrahedral forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pyritohedral class symmetry characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Pyritohedral crystals possess three cubic planes of symmetry but no dodecahedral planes; only three dyad axes coincide with the crystallographic axes; additionally there are three triad axes and a centre of symmetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although many forms are geometrically the same as holohedral class counterparts, face characters differ (striations), and hemihedral forms with parallel faces may be derived as positive/negative variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pentagonal dodecahedron identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Pentagonal dodecahedron is bounded by twelve non-regular pentagonal faces with three distinct edge sets; indices are {hko} and the simple form {210} is common in pyrites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not the regular geometric dodecahedron; recognize by pentagonal faces with unequal edge angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dyakis-dodecahedron identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Dyakis-dodecahedron is the hemihedral form of the hexakis-octahedron, bounded by twenty-four faces with indices {hkl}; as a simple form {321} occurs in pyrites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use face count (24) and relation to hexakis-octahedron to identify this hemihedral form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagihedral (gyroidal) class characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagihedral class has the full number of axes of symmetry (three tetrad, four triad, six dyad) but no planes of symmetry and no centre of symmetry; its unique simple form is the pentagonal icositetrahedron (twenty-four irregular pentagons) which is enantiomorphous (right- and left-handed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such enantiomorphic forms may rotate plane-polarized light; faces with high indices are rare and observed in a few salts and cuprite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tetartohedral class characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Tetartohedral class (tetrahedral pentagonal dodecahedral) has four polar triad axes and only three dyad axes (coinciding with crystallographic axes); several forms are geometrically similar to other cubic subclasses, while the general form is the tetrahedral pentagonal dodecahedron bounded by twelve irregular pentagons with multiple enantiomorphic variants ({hkl}, {khl}, {h'kl}, {k'hl}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize by the quarter-faced nature of the general hexakis-octahedron-derived form and by enantiomorphic pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tetragonal system definition and axial conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the tetragonal system the three axes are at right angles with two equal horizontal axes and a distinct vertical axis (parameters a:a:c). The unequal axis is the principal or morphological axis and is placed vertically; the axial ratio a:c (or c if a = 1) is characteristic of the substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cassiterite c = 0.67232, anatase c = 1.7771. Measure axial ratio to identify tetragonal minerals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holosymmetric (ditetragonal bipyramidal) tetragonal class
rubrics_metrics.description: This class has five planes of symmetry (one perpendicular to principal axis, four intersecting it) and five axes of symmetry (one tetrad and two pairs of dyad), plus a centre of symmetry; simple forms include tetragonal bipyramids of first and second order ({111}, {101}), ditetragonal bipyramid {hkl}, tetragonal prisms {110} or {100}, ditetragonal prism {hko}, and basal pinacoid {001}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify by plane and axis symmetries: presence of tetrad axis and specific combinations of bipyramids/prisms; the parametral plane {111} corresponds to face intercepts a : a : c.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tetragonal prism orders and indices
rubrics_metrics.description: Tetragonal prism of first order has faces intercepting equal lengths on horizontal axes and indices {110}; prism of second order has faces parallel to vertical axis and one horizontal axis with indices {100}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prisms are open forms and appear only in combination; equal-size {110} and {001} faces can make the figure geometrically a cube.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ditetragonal prism and basal pinacoid definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ditetragonal prism consists of eight faces parallel to principal axis intercepting horizontal axes in different lengths (indices {210}, {320}, etc., or {hko}). Basal pinacoid is a single pair of parallel faces perpendicular to the principal axis (indices {001}), an open form that exists only in combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intercept behavior with axes to assign these indices when analyzing crystal faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite symmetry (rotation with reflection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composite symmetry involves a rotation about an axis combined with a reflection across a plane so that a face on the upper half rotated and reflected falls into the position of a face on the lower half; used to describe some tetragonal bisphenoidal/hemihedral symmetries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize composite symmetry when identical face relations occur only after a combined rotation and reflection operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tetragonal bisphenoid and scalenohedron identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Bisphenoid is a double wedge bounded by four equal isosceles triangles with indices {111}, {211}, {112}, etc., or {hhl}; tetragonal scalenohedron (ditetragonal bisphenoid) is bounded by eight scalene triangles with indices {hkl} and may be considered hemihedral form of the ditetragonal bipyramid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms are identified by small face counts and wedge/double-wedge geometry; some minerals (chalcopyrite, stannite) exhibit combinations involving bisphenoids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthorhombic system definition and axial conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the orthorhombic system the three crystallographic axes are at right angles but of different lengths (parameters a : b : c). Conventionally the longer horizontal axis is taken as the macro-axis (b = 1) and the shorter horizontal axis as the brachy-axis (a), to define axial ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Axial ratios are constant for a substance and used to distinguish orthorhombic minerals (examples: barytes, anglesite, cerussite).

rubrics_metrics.name: Holohdral orthorhombic class symmetry and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: This class has three dissimilar dyad axes each coinciding with a crystallographic axis, three perpendicular dissimilar planes of symmetry, and a centre of symmetry. The general form is the bipyramid {hkl} (closed form bounded by eight scalene triangles); other open forms include prisms {110}, {210}, {120} ({hko}), macro- and brachy-prisms, and pinacoids {001}, {100}, {010}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine knowledge of axes, planes, and indices to identify orthorhombic crystals and their common combinations (figs. 56–59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro-prism and brachy-prism conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Macro-prism consists of four faces parallel to the macro-axis (indices {101}, {201} ... or {hol}); brachy-prism consists of four faces parallel to the brachy-axis (indices {011}, {021} ... or {okl}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are often called 'domes' and help describe prism orientation relative to the two horizontal axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthorhombic pyramid/hemimorphic and bisphenoidal classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Pyramidal class is hemimorphic with only one dyad axis and open pyramids {hkl} having four faces at one end; bisphenoidal class is hemihedral with three dyad axes but no planes or centre, general form {hkl} being a bisphenoid bounded by four scalene triangles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hemimorphism means different development at the two ends of the crystal (different faces/pedions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monoclinic system definition (angles and axes)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the monoclinic system two of the inter-axial angles are right angles while the third is oblique (beta); axes are unequal lengths. The ortho-axis OY = b is perpendicular to the other two; the clino-axis OX = a and vertical OZ = c lie in the plane of symmetry (choice of OX and OZ is somewhat arbitrary). Axial ratios a : b : c and beta are required to define the crystal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: gypsum, orthoclase, cane-sugar with specific axial ratios and beta angles. Beta determines whether hemi-pyramids lie in the acute or obtuse axial angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monoclinic holohedral class symmetry and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: This class has a single plane of symmetry with a dyad axis perpendicular to it and a centre of symmetry. The dyad axis coincides with the ortho-axis OY. Forms include clino-pinacoid {010}, ortho-pinacoid {100}, basal pinacoid {001}, clino-prisms {011} etc., prisms {110} etc., and hemi-pyramids {111} (distinguished as positive/negative by position in obtuse/acute angle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the plane-of-symmetry and axis coincidence to determine which pinacoid or prism indices are appropriate when classifying monoclinic crystals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monoclinic hemimorphic (sphenoidal) class
rubrics_metrics.description: In the hemimorphic monoclinic class the only element of symmetry is a single polar dyad axis; forms such as {010} (pedion) and its parallel {01'0} are dissimilar at the two ends; other pinacoids are geometrically the same as holohedral class forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enantiomorphism and polar dyad allow identification of right- and left-handed forms (e.g., tartaric acid crystals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinohedral monoclinic class (single plane symmetry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crystals symmetrical only with respect to a single plane; only clino-pinacoid {010} is geometrically the same as in holohedral class; other forms are pedions or domes ({hko}, {okl}, {hkl}) consisting of two planes equally inclined to the plane of symmetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize by absence of dyad axes/certain symmetries and by the presence of a single mirror plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anorthic/triclinic system definition
rubrics_metrics.description: In the anorthic (triclinic) system none of the three crystallographic axes are at right angles and they are all unequal in length; to define crystals here one needs a : b : c and the interaxial angles alpha, beta, gamma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Axial and angular constants (e.g., anorthite's values) are used to specify and identify triclinic crystals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holosymmetric triclinic class (pinacoidal)
rubrics_metrics.description: This class has only a centre of symmetry; all the forms are pinacoids (pairs of parallel faces), with pinacoids parallel to axial planes {100}, {010}, {001}, others indexed as {hko}, {hol}, {okl}, and general form {hkl}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect very simple face-pair morphology in holohedral triclinic crystals (pinacoidal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymmetric triclinic (pediad) class
rubrics_metrics.description: Crystals in this class lack any elements of symmetry; all forms are pedions (single planes) and the crystals are hemihedral relative to the holohedral triclinic class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite absence of symmetry, faces still arrange in zones; examples are rare and non-mineral examples are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hexagonal system axes and index conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Hexagonal system crystals are characterized by a single triad or hexad principal axis. Two axial representations are used: rhombohedral axes (three equal oblique axes equally inclined to principal axis) and hexagonal axes (four axes: three horizontal at 60° to one another and a vertical axis). Hexagonal indices are written {hikl} with h + i + k = 0 and axial ratio a : c characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose axis system appropriate to division (rhombohedral vs hexagonal); axial ratio examples: beryl a : c = 1 : 0.4989.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhombohedral division holosymmetric class and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: In the rhombohedral (trigonal) division the ho losymmetric class has a triad axis with three similar planes of symmetry inclined at 60°, three dyad axes perpendicular to those planes, and a centre of symmetry; simple forms include the rhombohedron (indices {100} and variants {hkk}) and scalenohedron (bounded by twelve scalene triangles, general indices {hkl}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhombohedra come in direct and inverse sets related by rotation about principal axis; scalenohedron relations with inscribed rhombohedron help identify faces and indices.
